headline: Learned models are refining cell type annotation across spatial and scRNA-seq data
label: Single Cell Type Annotation Methods
summary: Spatial and scRNA-seq studies now pair annotation, rare-population detection and gene selection with transformer, capsule and LLM models.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational assignment of cell identity in spatial and single-cell data, increasingly with learned or language-model components. Binary-SPA offers reference-free, marker-based annotation for high-resolution spatial transcriptomics, while a review of deep learning segmentation covers CNNs, transformers and foundation models for transcript-to-cell assignment. For scRNA-seq, CELLIA combines differential expression with curated tissue markers for LLM-based annotation, scKanFormer adds biologically informed attention in a Transformer-KAN model benchmarked against nine methods, and RareCapsNet targets rare populations with marker-gene explainability and cross-batch transfer. Upstream, SKIM and Principal Genes address dataset scale and feature selection. Qombucha extends deconvolution to glioblastoma methylation using a developmental hierarchy.
